source_review.notes: Checked six primary/official sources. GraphQL supports partial data plus path-addressed field errors and schema nullability propagation. AWS supports identifying core function, hard/soft dependencies, predictable degraded operation, and testing simpler fallback paths. Google SRE supports cheaper degraded modes, exercising overload paths, and shedding after degradation becomes insufficient. RFC 9457 supports typed machine-readable error responses and cautions against exposing implementation internals. RFC 9110 confirms 206 is range-response semantics, not generic application partial success.

evidence: Checked requested R, hard H, valid V, omitted/failed/pending O, coverage c, quality vector q/floor q_min, degradation duration T_d/T_max, fallback capacity B_f, and shifted load L_f for consistent set and unit meanings.
Confirmed completeness closure and minimum-useful conditions are separate.
Confirmed coverage count is explicitly insufficient for criticality/quality.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Quality-vector ordering is a design policy and not claimed to be a universal scalar metric.

evidence: Recounted product-page hard subset identity/price/purchasability and confirmed it is returned in the degraded example.
Confirmed batch outcomes 92+5+2+1 equal all 100 requested items.
Recomputed fallback overload 10,000-4,000 as 6,000/s and exercise primary/fallback gap 30,000-9,000 as 21,000/s.
Confirmed search coverage 45/50=90%, 12-minute stale age is within a 15-minute example ceiling, and exact ten examples/five answer pairs.
numerical_recomputation.notes: All capacities, ages, and component counts are labeled scenarios requiring domain evidence.

evidence: Verified V intersect O empty and V union O=R provide exactly one declared disposition in the closed-world model.
Verified H subset V plus per-component validity/quality is necessary for the defined minimum-useful result.
Constructed L>B_f counterexample showing existence of fallback does not prove graceful full traffic shift.
Constructed atomic A/B effect counterexample showing silent omission after A commits contradicts an all-or-none invariant.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The arguments do not claim completeness metadata alone proves correctness or authorization.

evidence: Reviewed ideal/minimum/invalid, partial/degraded/pending/failed, empty/null/absent/not-found/unauthorized/unavailable/stale/approximate/unknown distinctions.

Reviewed GraphQL field errors/null propagation, HTTP 200/202/206/error/problem semantics, batch item states, pagination/search coverage, streaming, legacy SDK/proxy/cache behavior, and capability negotiation.
Reviewed stale authorization/pricing/inventory, mixed snapshot, non-disclosure, fallback residency/security/audit, forged priority/cardinality, sensitive error details, and partial cache overwrite.
Reviewed primary/fallback/common-mode failures, overload, flag/control-plane loss, retry/hedge priority, timeout-after-commit, client crash, degradation duration, oscillation, and gradual recovery.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Coverage spans protocol, data quality, writes, security, clients, capacity, topology, and recovery.

evidence: Confirmed every finite requested component has exactly one declared disposition.
Confirmed hard components and quality/authorization floors cannot be degraded away.
Confirmed status, component state, provenance, freshness, coverage, and retry scope are machine-readable.
Confirmed atomic effects are never silently weakened and non-atomic batches preserve one authoritative item outcome.
Confirmed fallbacks have bounded independent capacity controls and degraded mode has observable entry/exit budgets.
invariant_checking.notes: No 2xx response is automatically counted as full-quality success.

evidence: Reviewed completeness closure and confirmed authorization/validity remain additional premises.
Reviewed minimum-useful argument and confirmed schema optionality is not substituted for business classification.
Reviewed fallback counterexample and confirmed reduced work/admission/provisioning is required when shifted load exceeds capacity.
Reviewed atomic-write argument and confirmed explicit non-atomic per-item contracts are the valid exception.
proof_review.notes: No fallback, stale cache, or approximation is claimed to preserve semantics without a domain floor.

evidence: Confirmed four arguments are labeled and assumptions are adjacent.
Confirmed GraphQL, HTTP, problem-details, AWS, and Google SRE behavior is attributed to source scope.
Confirmed example response modes, capacities, ages, and rollout percentages are design scenarios rather than standards.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Protocol rules, domain policy, and empirical capacity/quality obligations remain distinct.

evidence: All six primary/official references were checked on 2026-09-02 where current guidance applies.
All counts, rates, ages, capacities, coverage, and recovery cohorts are labeled examples.

Actual minimum usefulness, client handling, quality harm, fallback independence/capacity, stale safety, dependency combinations, resource reduction, and recovery stability remain explicit product/security/integration/load/fault evidence obligations.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No production workflow, client fleet, fallback system, or user-quality threshold was empirically assessed.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed minimum truth, result categories, hard/soft dependencies, completeness, protocol representation, GraphQL locality, write/batch truth, stale/approximate modes, fallback capacity, client evolution, deadlines, security, mode lifecycle, observability, and fault verification as one degradation contract.

practitioner_review.notes: Checked implementability through degradation matrices, closed component dispositions, stable typed errors, per-item identity/outcomes, provenance/quality floors, separate cache modes, capability negotiation, bounded fallback controls, local-safe flags, cohort recovery, and full-versus-degraded SLIs.

pedagogical_review.notes: The module develops degradation from minimum useful truth through response and write semantics, then stale/approximate/fallback/client/security concerns, mode recovery, observability, and verification. Ten examples and five integrative exercises have complete answers.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed.
